guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the sim has TWO potion-procure paths and only the out-of-combat one consults should_procure_potion, so a mid-combat Alchemize gives a Sozu owner a potion the game refuses
guards.issue: MECHANISM: in C# there is exactly ONE procure entry point -- PotionCmd.TryToProcure (PotionCmd.cs:27-52) -- and its first statement is the Hook.ShouldProcurePotion gate (PotionCmd.cs:31); an executed grep finds all ten callers go through it (PotionReward, MerchantPotionEntry, AlchemicalCoffer, DelicateFrond, PhialHolster, EntropicBrew, Alchemize, the console and the multiplayer synchroniser). The sim splits the operation: RunState.add_potion (run.py:474-485) runs the gate, but PlayerCombatState.add_potion (player.py:107-121) does NOT -- its own docstring concedes it at player.py:112-115. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-sozu): `RunState.add_potion` with Sozu held returns kept=False and an empty belt (correct), while `PlayerCombatState.add_potion` with the same relic returns kept=True and belt ['fire_potion', None, None] where C# refuses. Both sides are ported content: Sozu comes from the ported Darv shrine (events/darv.py) and the ungated path has FOUR ported callers, printed by the probe -- cards/colorless_skills.py:53 (Alchemize, a ported Colorless Skill that generates a random combat potion), potions.py:1217 (Entropic Brew), relics/delicate_frond.py:25 and relics/petrified_toad.py:20. SCOPE NOTE: the shared contract defers potions, but this is not a potion-content audit finding -- it is a relic whose entire stated effect is the gate, and the divergent observable is the potion BELT, which the conformance runner asserts and resyncs slot-by-slot. Same reasoning as relic/belt_buckle's AfterPotionProcured entry, which likewise filed rather than waived.

guards.what: N1: `return player != base.Owner;` (Sozu.cs:17-20) vs the sim's unconditional `return False` (sozu.py:27); and the same missing owner check on ModifyMaxEnergy (Sozu.cs:24-27)
guards.rationale: Both are multiplayer owner filters. C#'s ShouldProcurePotion is dispatched over every listener in the run including other players' relics, so `player != Owner` means 'only refuse MY potions'; with one player that expression is constantly False, which is exactly what sozu.py:27 returns. The sim's own hook signature has no player parameter at all (relics/base.py:217-220), so the distinction is unrepresentable and unneeded. Waived as multiplayer-only under the shared contract's global scope, not under an unreachability claim about ported content.

guards.rationale: Checked against PROMPT.md bug class 13 and sweep A: Sozu.cs declares no field beyond the two overrides and sozu.py adds nothing to __init__, so there is no latched state to carry across a combat boundary.
